intro: In central Roi Et, where most options are plain hotel blocks, Rueanrimnam Hotel (the Thai name means "riverside house") is a small 33-room boutique that guests remember for its garden-home feel and easy-going service · It sits on Charoen Panit Road in the town centre, within walking distance of Wat Burapha Phiram, Roi Et National Museum and Bueng Phlan Chai · There's free Thai breakfast, free parking, and rates from approx. ฿500/night · Real guest reviews agree the staff are lovely and the breakfast is better than the price suggests — though there are a few limitations worth knowing before you book.

body.html: Rueanrimnam Hotel is a small 33-room boutique property in central Roi Et, on Charoen Panit Road in the Nai Mueang subdistrict · The Thai name, "riverside house," speaks to the garden-home concept rather than an actual river view — the hotel is in the town centre, not on an open waterfront · What sets it apart from the usual city blocks is its easy-going feel and small scale, making it feel more like staying with relatives than at a business hotel.

Rooms range from Superior and Deluxe to a roomier VIP category · What guests consistently praise is that the rooms are clean, quiet and the beds easy to sleep in, especially the VIP rooms that several reviews call larger than the price suggests · Every room has air conditioning, a refrigerator, free bottled water and free Wi-Fi · In-room kit is basic but functional — not luxurious, but a good fit for a few hundred baht in central Roi Et.
"The staff are so lovely, the room clean and quiet · the Thai breakfast was tastier than expected — at a few hundred baht in central Roi Et it's good value."

The two things reviews mention most are the Thai breakfast and the staff · Many guests say the breakfast is freshly made, home-style and included with the room, while the English-speaking reception is helpful enough to bring people back for repeat stays · There's a restaurant, a coffee shop, a small garden, massage service and free on-site parking — handy if you're driving yourself or stopping over on an Isan trip.

The location is in central Roi Et: it's a roughly 15-minute walk to Wat Burapha Phiram (home to a tall standing Buddha) and Roi Et National Museum, and not far from Bueng Phlan Chai, the lake park in the heart of town · Eateries and convenience stores surround the hotel, so food is easy to find · Roi Et Airport is about 14 km away, with a paid airport shuttle available.

To be straight with you, per real guest reviews: the limitations mentioned are that this is a basic hotel with no lift and no in-room tea/coffee · Some reviews describe the beds as fairly firm, Thai-style · On location, while you can walk to the sights, the side street is fairly quiet and a few guests found it feels deserted at night · A couple of reviews also mention noise from a nearby nightlife venue on some nights, so ask for an inner room if you're a light sleeper.

In short: if you want a place in central Roi Et that's friendly, clean, with free Thai breakfast, at a few hundred baht, and you don't mind the lack of a lift or full hotel facilities — Rueanrimnam Hotel is a fitting choice · The 7.7 from 13 Trip.com reviews, plus the #1 Specialty lodging ranking in Roi Et on TripAdvisor, captures it well: small, friendly, good value · It suits temple visitors, museum-goers, or anyone stopping over for a night on an Isan trip.

A tip from following the reviews here: if you want a roomier stay, ask about the VIP room at the time of booking, since many guests say it's worth the small price bump · And don't skip the Thai breakfast — it's the single most-mentioned highlight · If you sleep lightly, request an inner room away from the road and any nightlife.

honestSummary: Rueanrimnam Hotel is the best pick for travellers who want a friendly, clean in-town Roi Et stay with free Thai breakfast, at just a few hundred baht — a small garden-home feel, lovely staff, walkable to Wat Burapha Phiram and Bueng Phlan Chai · You just have to accept it's a basic hotel with no lift and minimal in-room amenities.
honestChecks: If you want the full facilities of a large hotel — this is a basic 33-room boutique with no lift and no in-room tea/coffee → for a pool, gym or fully kitted rooms, look at a larger city hotel.
If you're a light sleeper — a few reviews mention noise from a nearby nightlife venue on some nights → request an inner room away from the road when you book.
If you're concerned about walking around at night — the side street is fairly quiet and some guests found it feels deserted after dark → plan to use a car or Grab for evening outings.

faq.q: Where is Rueanrimnam Hotel in Roi Et, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Rueanrimnam Hotel is at 72 Charoen Panit Road, Nai Mueang subdistrict, in central Roi Et · It's about a 15-minute walk to Wat Burapha Phiram (home to a tall standing Buddha) and Roi Et National Museum, and not far from Bueng Phlan Chai and Roi Et Tower (Ho Hoht 101) in the heart of town · Eateries and convenience stores surround the hotel, so food is easy to find.

faq.q: How much does Rueanrimnam Hotel cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿500/night for a Superior Room · Deluxe and the roomier VIP run about ฿600–฿800 · Prices vary by room type and season, so compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does Rueanrimnam Hotel have breakfast, and is it any good?
faq.a: Yes · There's a free Thai breakfast included with the room, and it's the most-mentioned highlight in the reviews — freshly made, home-style and good value · It's served in the hotel's small restaurant with an easy-going feel.

faq.q: Does Rueanrimnam Hotel have a lift, and is it suitable for older guests?
faq.a: There's no lift · Upper-floor rooms mean stairs, so request a ground-floor room if you're with elderly relatives or heavy bags · It's a small, basic hotel without the full facilities of a larger property.

faq.q: Who is Rueanrimnam Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers who want a friendly, clean in-town Roi Et stay with free Thai breakfast, at a few hundred baht · It suits couples, solo travellers and self-drivers who want free parking · It's less suited to those who need a lift or the full facilities of a larger hotel.

faq.q: Is Rueanrimnam Hotel quiet, or is there any noise?
faq.a: Most rooms are quiet and clean, but a few reviews mention noise from a nearby nightlife venue on some nights, and the side street is quiet enough that some guests found it feels deserted late at night · If you sleep lightly, request an inner room away from the road, and plan to use a car or Grab for evening outings.
